chunks: Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr al-Nadhr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' experiences menstruation before she performs Tawaf al-Ifadah (the circumambulation for release from Ihram), so her purity occurs on the night of Arafah.' He said: 'If she knows that she will be pure, perform Tawaf al-Ifadah with the House, and be released from her Ihram, and join the people at Mina, then let her do so.'

key_terms.تَحِلُّ مِنْ إِحْرَامِهَا: She is released from the state of Ihram.
key_terms.تَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ: She performs circumambulation around the Kaaba (specifically Tawaf al-Ifadah).
key_terms.تَلْحَقُ النَّاسَ بِمِنًى: She joins the pilgrims at Mina.
key_terms.طُهْرُهَا: Her state of purity from menstruation.
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: The night of the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah, after sunset on Arafah day.
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعَةً: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in a single journey with a break in Ihram between them.

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she starts menstruating before completing Tawaf al-Ifadah during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in Hajj al-Tamattu' rituals when a woman’s menstruation coincides with the critical window of the night of Arafah. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits her to perform Tawaf al-Ifadah upon purity even if it occurs late, allowing her to join the communal rites at Mina without invalidating her Hajj, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (*taysir*) in ritual obligations. This ruling underscores the distinction between the essential pillars of Hajj and the conditions of purity, ensuring that temporary impurity does not obstruct the completion of the pilgrimage.
